name: NCD gold questions
description: Grounded evaluation questions for the WHO NCD Guideline Tutor. expected_doc_ids are catalog ids, not filenames. expected_doc_ids are acceptable document alternatives for hit rate. expected_sources are acceptable (doc_id, 1-based PDF page) alternatives; missing annotations are unscored. ncd_type is a descriptive label; only filters configures retrieval.

cases.question: At what blood pressure threshold does WHO recommend initiating pharmacological treatment for hypertension in adults?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: with a confirmed diagnosis of hypertension and systolic blood pressure of ≥140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure of ≥90 mmHg.
with a confirmed diagnosis of hypertension and systolic blood pressure of ≥140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure of ≥90 mmHg.

cases.question: Should adults with existing cardiovascular disease and systolic blood pressure 130–139 mmHg receive antihypertensive medication according to WHO?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: WHO recommends pharmacological antihypertensive treatment of individuals with existing cardiovascular disease and systolic blood pressure of 130–139 mmHg.

cases.question: Does WHO require laboratory tests before starting pharmacological therapy for hypertension?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: but only when testing does not delay or impede starting treatment.

cases.question: What target blood pressure does the WHO hypertension guideline recommend for adults on pharmacological treatment?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: WHO recommends a target blood pressure treatment goal of <140/90 mmHg in all patients with hypertension without comorbidities.

cases.question: What does WHO say about combination therapy versus monotherapy when starting hypertension treatment?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: WHO suggests combination therapy, preferably with a single-pill combination (to improve adherence and persistence), as an initial treatment.

cases.question: Can nonphysician health workers initiate and manage pharmacological treatment of hypertension according to WHO?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: proper training, prescribing authority, specific management protocols and physician oversight.

cases.question: How frequently should blood pressure be reassessed after starting or intensifying antihypertensive medication?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: WHO suggests a monthly follow up after initiation or a change in antihypertensive medications until patients reach target.

cases.question: What diagnostic criteria and tests does HEARTS-D use to diagnose diabetes?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: Diagnosis of diabetes is based on values of plasma glucose or glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c).

cases.question: What is the recommended initial pharmacological treatment for type 2 diabetes when diet and physical activity are not enough?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: Metformin does not cause weight gain or hypoglycaemia and is the recommended initial treatment for people who do not achieve the desired glycaemic control with diet and physical activity.
Metformin is recommended as the first-line drug in the treatment of diabetes.

cases.question: When is metformin contraindicated in the HEARTS-D diabetes protocol?
How much weekly physical activity does HEARTS-D recommend for adults with type 2 diabetes?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: Most adults should engage in at least 150 minutes of moderate or vigorous-intensity aerobic activity per week, spread over at least 3 days.

cases.question: What does the HEARTS-D annex say about treating type 2 diabetes with insulin?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: Annex 1: Protocol for treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus with insulin

cases.question: What are the sample HEARTS hypertension treatment protocols, including first-line diuretic use?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: The following pages outline sample protocols for managing hypertension, each with a different starting medication.

cases.question: According to HEARTS evidence-based treatment protocols, when should blood pressure be measured?

expected_sources.evidence_excerpt: Blood pressure measurements should be conducted on adults during routine visits to primary health care facilities, including all adults at first presentation to the facility, and, if normal, periodically thereafter

annotation_metadata.method: Assistant review of local PDF text; not independent clinical expert review.
annotation_metadata.page_convention: 1-based PDF page index, not printed page labels.
annotation_metadata.scope: Known supporting pages, not an exhaustive list of every valid source. A source hit may cover only part of a multi-part question. Source precision is annotation agreement, not clinical correctness.
annotation_metadata.normalization: Unicode NFKC and collapsed whitespace for excerpt validation.
